name: addpipe24_radix4_sparse_tree
rationale: Empirically, flat multi-term SOP expressions consistently beat explicitly staged 2-input prefix stages at the same granularity (cla_block4 flat beat cla_block4_kstree; cla_block3_flat beat cla_block3_kstree), while full bit-level Kogge-Stone matched baseline WNS (7.517) at high area cost (549.8) because every one of its 5 stages is a separate 2-input combine touching all 24 bits. This candidate fuses KS's first two stride-1/stride-2 stages into a single flat radix-4 (per-4-bit-group) generate/propagate SOP -- reusing the proven-efficient block-G/P style -- and then performs a proper doubling prefix tree with only 3 remaining 2-input stages (stride 4, 8, 16) instead of 5, correctly covering full 24-bit cumulative carry generation. This should retain near-KS logical depth/WNS (since the flat 4-input SOP collapses two KS levels into one that ABC can rebalance freely, matching the win pattern already observed for flat-vs-staged CLA), while cutting total combine-node count relative to full bit-level KS (only 3 full-width prefix passes instead of 5), targeting a new non-dominated area/WNS point closer to baseline (530.936/7.51866) than any custom adder tried so far.
